blocks.content: Earthquakes do not kill people; it is unsafe buildings and unreinforced structures that cause casualties.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India is classified into four seismic zones (Zone II to Zone V), with Zone V representing the highest seismic hazard.
Over 59% of India's landmass is prone to earthquakes of moderate to very high intensity.
Earthquake mitigation strategies include structural measures like base isolation and retrofitting, alongside non-structural land-use planning.
The National Disaster Management Guidelines emphasize microzonation and strict enforcement of building codes.
Zone V includes the entire North-East India, parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Rann of Kutch, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
IS 1893 is the primary BIS code governing earthquake-resistant design of structures in India.
Richter scale measures magnitude (energy released), whereas Modified Mercalli scale measures intensity (observed damage).
